{{NSE|GTLINFRA}} | logo = GTL_Infrastructure_official_logo.jpg | logo_size = 200px | key_people = | founded = 2004[https://www.livemint.com/Companies/CyCJbr1f47LSxBm3SDM24H/GTL-Infra-stake-sale-likely-to-value-firm-at-Rs11000-crore.html GTL Infra founded in 2004] | hq_location = [[Navi Mumbai]], India | products = [[Network service provider|Network Services Provider]] | revenue = | operating_income = | net_income = | assets = | equity = | num_employees = 1075 [https://www.gtlinfra.com/wp-content/uploads/pdf/14th-Annual-Report-2016-17-with-AGM-Notice.pdf 14th Annual Report 2016-17 with AGM Notice] | owner = | parent = | divisions = | subsidiaries = | industry = | services = | website = [http://www.gtlinfra.com GTL Infrastructure Limited] }} '''GTL Infrastructure Limited''' (GTL Infra) is an Indian telecom tower company that focuses on shared passive telecom infrastructure. Headquartered in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, GTL Infra operates approximately 28,000 towers across 22 telecom circles in India, facilitating the provision of 2G, 3G, and 4G services by telecom service providers.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/aboutgtl.cms |title=About GTL Infrastructure |publisher=Economictimes Indiatimes |access-date=28 November 2017}} It was incorporated in 2004 by [[Manoj G. Tirodkar]], who serves as the chairman of the company.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/gtl-infrastructure-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-16883.cms |title=GTL Infrastructure Ltd. |publisher=Economictimes Indiatimes |access-date=17 November 2017}} ==History== In 2006, GTL Infra was listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] (BSE) and the [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange]] (NSE), becoming the first company in India’s shared telecom infrastructure sector to be publicly listed. The following year, GTL Infra launched a rights issue valued at US$83.86 million. In 2010, the company acquired 17,500 towers and 21,000 tenants from [[Aircel]].{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/info-tech/gtl-infrachennai-network-combined-debt-falls-to-rs-4193-cr/article9767686.ece |title=GTL Infra-Chennai Network combined debt falls to Rs. 4,193 cr |publisher=The Hindu Business Line |access-date=14 November 2017}} GTL Infra was also affected by the cancellation of licenses, as its customer base decreased due to issues faced by Aircel and Maxis, along with the subsequent cancellation of the [[Right of first refusal|Right of First Refusal]] (ROFR) by [[Aircel]]. In the subsequent years, GTL Infra undertook [[debt restructuring]] efforts. ==Listing== The company's equity shares are listed on the [[National Stock Exchange of India|National Stock Exchange of India Limited]] (NSE) and the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] (BSE). Additionally, its [[Foreign currency convertible bonds|Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds]] are listed on the [[Singapore Exchange|Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited]].{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/stock-markets/21-cos-may-default-on-fccb-commitments-sp/article3555408.ece |title=21 cos may default on FCCB commitments: S&P |publisher=The Hindu Business Line |date=21 Jun 2012|access-date=14 November 2017}} ==Services== GTL Infra owns urban and rural telecom towers located in all the 22 telecom circles in India, which are shared by all telecom operators in the country. GTL Infra also offers real-time monitoring from its NOC (Network Operations Centre) and operations and maintenance services.{{cite web|url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/article/news-top-story/reliance-jio-and-gtl-infra-sign-tower-infrastructure-sharing-deal-116092000305_1.html |title=Reliance Jio and GTL Infra sign Tower Infrastructure Sharing Deal |publisher=indiainfoline.com |date=20 September 2016 |access-date=2012-11-03}} ==Awards & Recognition== * GTL Infra received the Best Infrastructure Brands award from
